exclusions.reason: Separate later spec; this spec covers only the employee questionnaire.

feature.title: Employee onboarding questionnaire
feature.goal: A new employee answers one short, conditional English questionnaire once, and Lonio records exactly the data that Pensionskasse Muster, source tax (the Zurich tariff) and Muster AG HR need for that person. From the answers it derives the insurance start date and the full source tax tariff code, and it collects no personal data that no party needs.

sections.title: Personal details and home address
sections.purpose: Collect the employee's name, date of birth and complete postal address, which also gives the country of residence, and the canton for Swiss residents, so the fund can register the employee and HR can post documents.

stories.title: Personal details for the pension fund registration
stories.i_want: the new employee's first name, last name and date of birth
stories.so_that: the new employee can be registered as an insured person. The registration form does not accept any of these fields empty.
stories.priority_reason: All three are required fields on the pension fund's registration form. The form cannot be submitted while any of them is empty, so a missing value blocks the registration.

acceptance_criteria.title: Name is asked of every employee and is required
acceptance_criteria.given: a new employee is filling in the onboarding questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.when: they reach the personal details at the start of the questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.then: they are asked for their first name and their last name. Both are required, so the questionnaire cannot be submitted while either is empty. Both answers are recorded for the pension fund registration.

acceptance_criteria.title: Date of birth is asked of every employee as a date
acceptance_criteria.given: a new employee is filling in the personal details
acceptance_criteria.when: they give their date of birth
acceptance_criteria.then: the date of birth is required and is given as a date in the form DD.MM.YYYY, the form the pension fund uses. The questionnaire cannot be submitted without it. It is recorded for the pension fund registration.

stories.title: Complete home address for posting documents
stories.i_want: the new employee's complete home address: street, house number, postcode, town and country
stories.so_that: documents posted to the employee reach them
stories.priority_reason: HR posts many documents to employees and says the address 'has to be complete'. An incomplete address stops documents from reaching the employee.

acceptance_criteria.title: All parts of the address are asked and required
acceptance_criteria.given: a new employee is filling in the onboarding questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.when: they reach the home address step, which follows the personal details
acceptance_criteria.then: they are asked for street, house number, postcode, town and country, and each part is required. The questionnaire cannot be submitted while any part is empty. The address is recorded for HR.

acceptance_criteria.title: Address is a normal postal address and nothing more
acceptance_criteria.given: a new employee is giving their home address
acceptance_criteria.when: they fill in the home address step
acceptance_criteria.then: they are asked only for what a normal postal address on an envelope needs: street, house number, postcode, town and country. No other address details are asked. The country is given by its English name, e.g. Switzerland, Germany or Liechtenstein.

stories.title: Home address country is the country of residence for later questions
stories.i_want: the country of the employee's home address to be used as their country of residence
stories.so_that: Lonio knows whether the employee lives abroad, and so is always subject to source tax, without asking for the residence a second time
stories.priority_reason: Today HR decides source tax liability by hand, and living abroad is the first criterion. Lonio also derives the calculator's residence answers from this country, so getting it wrong blocks the correct tariff code.

acceptance_criteria.title: Residence is asked once, as part of the address
acceptance_criteria.given: a new employee has given the country of their home address
acceptance_criteria.when: later parts of the questionnaire need their country of residence
acceptance_criteria.then: that country counts as their country of residence. The employee is not asked separately whether their main residence is in Switzerland or which state they live in. The country is recorded for HR and for source tax.

acceptance_criteria.title: Living abroad makes the employee subject to source tax, and residence decides the follow-up questions
acceptance_criteria.given: a new employee has given the country of their home address
acceptance_criteria.when: the country is not Switzerland
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee is treated as living abroad and is subject to source tax whatever their nationality, so they are not asked about Swiss citizenship or the canton. If the country is Switzerland, they are asked for the canton and about Swiss citizenship.

examples.name: Employee living in another country, e.g. France (illustrative)

stories.title: Canton of residence for employees living in Switzerland
stories.i_want: the canton of employees who live in Switzerland
stories.so_that: the required 'Canton' field of the registration can be filled
stories.priority_reason: 'Canton' is a required field on the pension fund's registration form. The form cannot be submitted while it is empty, so a missing canton blocks the registration.

acceptance_criteria.title: Canton is asked only of residents of Switzerland and is then required
acceptance_criteria.given: a new employee has given the country of their home address
acceptance_criteria.when: they continue the home address step
acceptance_criteria.then: if the country is Switzerland, they are asked which canton they live in, and an answer is required. If the country is any other country, the canton is not asked. What the fund expects for employees living abroad, and whether 'Canton' means residence or work, is still open (see OQ-canton-abroad).

acceptance_criteria.title: Canton is chosen from the fund's list of the 26 Swiss cantons
acceptance_criteria.given: a new employee living in Switzerland is asked for their canton
acceptance_criteria.when: they answer
acceptance_criteria.then: they choose one of the 26 Swiss cantons that the pension fund lists: Aargau, Appenzell Ausserrhoden, Appenzell Innerrhoden, Basel-Landschaft, Basel-Stadt, Bern, Fribourg, Geneva, Glarus, Graubünden, Jura, Lucerne, Neuchâtel, Nidwalden, Obwalden, Schaffhausen, Schwyz, Solothurn, St. Gallen, Thurgau, Ticino, Uri, Valais, Vaud, Zug or Zurich. The canton is recorded for the pension fund registration.

sections.title: First working day and insurance start date
sections.purpose: Ask the employee for the first working day and derive the pension fund insurance start date from it, so that the start date always falls on the 1st of a month and follows the latest first working day.

stories.title: Employee enters the first working day
stories.i_want: every new employee to enter and confirm their own first working day in the onboarding questionnaire
stories.so_that: the start of employment is recorded from the person who knows the latest date, and the pension fund registration has the basis for the insurance start date
stories.priority_reason: HR calls the first working day 'the number one thing'; it changes often, and an outdated date has already caused a wrong insurance start and weeks of fixing (Julia).

acceptance_criteria.title: First working day is always asked and required
acceptance_criteria.given: any new employee fills in the onboarding questionnaire, whatever their residence, nationality or family situation
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee reaches the employment step
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee is asked for their first working day at Muster AG as a date (DD.MM.YYYY) and cannot submit the questionnaire without it

acceptance_criteria.title: The employee confirms the date themselves
acceptance_criteria.given: the first working day often moves before the start (e.g. the employee negotiates an earlier exit with the old employer)
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee answers the first working day question
acceptance_criteria.then: the date the employee enters is the one recorded for HR and used as the basis for the pension fund insurance start date; the employee is not asked for the insurance start date itself

acceptance_criteria.title: After submission only HR changes the date; the latest date counts
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee has submitted the questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.when: the first working day moves afterwards
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee can no longer change it in the questionnaire; the change is made by HR (specified in the later HR-side spec), only the latest date is kept, with no history of earlier dates, and everything derived from it uses the latest date

stories.title: Insurance start date derived from the first working day
stories.i_want: the insurance start date to be derived from the employee's latest first working day and always fall on the 1st of a month
stories.so_that: the employee is registered with the correct insurance start date, even when the first working day moves
stories.priority_reason: A start date that did not follow a moved first working day (Julia) led to a wrong insurance start at the fund, an unfriendly letter and weeks of fixing; the fund's field is required and must be the 1st of a month.

acceptance_criteria.title: First working day on the 1st of a month
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee's first working day is the 1st of a month
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio derives the insurance start date
acceptance_criteria.then: the insurance starts on the first working day itself

acceptance_criteria.title: First working day on any other day
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee's first working day is not the 1st of a month
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio derives the insurance start date
acceptance_criteria.then: the insurance starts on the 1st of the following month, also across a year end

examples.name: Start on the 2nd of a month

acceptance_criteria.title: Insurance start date always follows the latest first working day
acceptance_criteria.given: the first working day has been changed (before submission by the employee, after submission by HR)
acceptance_criteria.when: the insurance start date is needed for the pension fund
acceptance_criteria.then: it is derived again from the latest first working day, never from an earlier one, and it is not asked from the employee

sections.title: Civil status and spouse for the pension fund
sections.purpose: Ask the civil status once. Map it to the fund's list and to married/single for source tax. Ask the spouse's or partner's date of birth only where the fund requires it.

stories.title: Ask the civil status once, using the pension fund's list
stories.i_want: to state my civil status once, choosing from a list that also covers registered partnership and separation
stories.so_that: I am not asked the same thing again for the pension fund and for source tax, and my real situation can be recorded
stories.priority_reason: The pension fund's 'Civil status' field is required, so the registration cannot go ahead without it. Source tax needs it as well to decide married or single.

acceptance_criteria.title: Civil status is asked of every employee and is required
acceptance_criteria.given: a new employee is filling in the onboarding questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.when: they reach the family step
acceptance_criteria.then: Lonio asks for their civil status. The question cannot be left empty. Lonio asks it only once, and the same answer is used for the pension fund and, if the employee is subject to source tax, for source tax.

acceptance_criteria.title: Allowed civil status values
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee is asked for their civil status
acceptance_criteria.when: they choose an answer
acceptance_criteria.then: they can choose exactly one of these: Single, Married, Divorced, Widowed, Registered partnership, Separated. The first four use the wording of the pension fund's list. Registered partnership and Separated are added so that a partnered or separated employee does not have to pick a value that does not describe them.

stories.title: Ask the spouse's or partner's date of birth from married, partnered and separated employees
stories.i_want: to receive the date of birth of the husband, wife or registered partner of every employee who is registered with me as Married
stories.so_that: the registration is not rejected with 'Spouse's date of birth is required'
stories.priority_reason: The fund rejects a Married registration when the spouse's date of birth is missing, so the registration is blocked without it.

acceptance_criteria.title: Asked and required only for Married, Registered partnership and Separated
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee has stated their civil status
acceptance_criteria.when: the civil status is Married, Registered partnership or Separated
acceptance_criteria.then: Lonio asks for the date of birth of the spouse or registered partner. For separated employees this is the spouse they are separated from. The answer is required, and it is recorded for the pension fund. Single, divorced and widowed employees are not asked. Whether the fund needs anything for Divorced or Widowed is still open (see OQ-spouse-dob-other-status), and so is the provisional handling of partnered and separated employees (see OQ-civil-status-partnership).

acceptance_criteria.title: Form of the date
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee is asked for the spouse's or partner's date of birth
acceptance_criteria.when: they enter it
acceptance_criteria.then: the date is given as day, month and year (DD.MM.YYYY), as the pension fund expects it.

acceptance_criteria.title: Spouse's date of birth is discarded when it no longer applies
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee entered a spouse's date of birth and then changed their civil status to Single, Divorced or Widowed
acceptance_criteria.when: they submit the questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.then: the spouse's date of birth is not kept. While the employee is still moving back and forth in the questionnaire, the entered date is kept, so it is not lost if they switch back.

stories.title: Enter the civil status in the pension fund's terms
stories.i_want: every employee's civil status to be recorded as one of the values on my list: Single, Married, Divorced or Widowed
stories.so_that: the employee can be registered even when they are in a registered partnership or separated, which my list does not offer
stories.priority_reason: The fund's field is required and offers only four values. Without a mapping, partnered and separated employees (for example Daniel) cannot be registered.

acceptance_criteria.title: Civil status for the pension fund
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee has stated their civil status
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio records the civil status for the pension fund
acceptance_criteria.then: Single, Married, Divorced and Widowed are recorded unchanged. Registered partnership is provisionally recorded as Married, together with the partner's date of birth. Separated is provisionally recorded as Married, together with the date of birth of the spouse they are separated from. Both provisional mappings still have to be checked with a domain expert and the fund (see OQ-civil-status-partnership). The fund's civil status is always derived again from the latest civil status.

stories.title: Group the civil status for source tax
stories.i_want: each employee's civil status to be sorted into one of the calculator's two groups: 'married or registered partnership' or 'single, divorced, separated or widowed'
stories.so_that: the tariff code, the spouse exemption and the follow-up source tax questions use the calculator's logic
stories.priority_reason: Lonio now computes the tariff code itself instead of HR using the calculator. A wrong group gives a wrong tariff letter.

acceptance_criteria.title: Civil status group for source tax
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee has stated their civil status
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio derives the civil status for source tax
acceptance_criteria.then: Married and Registered partnership count as 'married or registered partnership'. Registered partners therefore also qualify for the spouse exemption. Single, Divorced, Widowed and Separated count as 'single, divorced, separated or widowed'. Separated employees therefore get no spouse exemption. The group is always derived again from the latest civil status.

acceptance_criteria.title: Separated: Married for the fund, single for source tax
acceptance_criteria.given: a separated employee
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio derives the civil status for each party
acceptance_criteria.then: the pension fund gets Married (provisional, see OQ-civil-status-partnership), and source tax counts the employee as single. Both results come from the one civil status answer; the employee is not asked anything twice.

sections.title: Source tax liability check
sections.purpose: Decide from residence, Swiss citizenship, C permit and the spouse exemption whether the employee is subject to source tax. Ask these facts only as far as they are needed, so that only employees subject to source tax get the source tax questions.

stories.title: Ask Swiss citizenship and C permit only of employees living in Switzerland
stories.i_want: to be asked whether I am a Swiss citizen and, if I am not, whether I hold a C permit, but only when I live in Switzerland and never for my full nationality or any other permit type
stories.so_that: Lonio learns exactly what decides my source tax liability without collecting personal data that no receiving party needs
stories.priority_reason: Swiss citizenship and C permit decide source tax liability. Today HR works this out by hand and does not know in advance who has to answer the source tax questions (F-hr_transcript-b6d9b3, F-hr_transcript-b84498).

acceptance_criteria.title: Swiss citizenship is asked only of employees living in Switzerland
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee has entered the country of their home address
acceptance_criteria.when: the country is Switzerland
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee is asked whether they hold Swiss citizenship, with the answers "yes" or "no", and must answer. Employees whose home address is in another country are not asked, because they are subject to source tax whatever their nationality. The answer is recorded for source tax, and for HR to decide whether the permit reminder is shown.

acceptance_criteria.title: Dual citizens answer as Swiss citizens
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee living in Switzerland holds Swiss citizenship and also another nationality
acceptance_criteria.when: they answer the Swiss citizenship question
acceptance_criteria.then: they answer "yes". Anyone with Swiss citizenship counts as Swiss for source tax. Their other nationality is not asked.

acceptance_criteria.title: C permit is asked only of non-Swiss employees living in Switzerland
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee lives in Switzerland
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee has answered that they do not hold Swiss citizenship
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee is asked whether they hold a C permit (permanent residence), with the answers "yes" or "no", and must answer. Swiss citizens and employees living abroad are not asked. No other permit type is asked. The answer is recorded for source tax.

stories.title: Ask spouse details only when the spouse could exempt the employee
stories.i_want: to know whether a married or registered-partner employee's spouse or partner is Swiss or holds a C permit, and whether they live in Switzerland, but only when this can change the employee's source tax liability
stories.so_that: employees exempted through their spouse, such as Tomás, are not wrongly treated as subject to source tax, and no spouse data is collected when it cannot change the result
stories.priority_reason: HR's real case Tomás shows that leaving out the spouse leads to the wrong liability decision (F-hr_transcript-d7431e). HR states which spouse facts are needed (F-hr_transcript-f3ce84).

acceptance_criteria.title: Spouse's Swiss citizenship is asked only when the spouse could exempt the employee
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee lives in Switzerland, is not a Swiss citizen and holds no C permit
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee's civil status is Married or Registered partnership
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee is asked whether their spouse or registered partner holds Swiss citizenship ("yes" or "no"; dual citizens count as "yes") and must answer. It is not asked of Single, Divorced, Widowed or Separated employees, because separated employees count as single for source tax. It is not asked of employees who are Swiss, hold a C permit or live abroad. The answer is recorded for source tax.

acceptance_criteria.title: Spouse's C permit is asked only for a non-Swiss spouse
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee has been asked about their spouse's or partner's Swiss citizenship
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee answers that the spouse or partner is not a Swiss citizen
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee is asked whether the spouse or partner holds a C permit (permanent residence), with the answers "yes" or "no", and must answer. No other permit type is asked. When the spouse is Swiss, this question is not asked. The answer is recorded for source tax.

acceptance_criteria.title: Spouse's residence is asked only for a Swiss or C-permit spouse
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee has stated that their spouse or partner is a Swiss citizen or holds a C permit
acceptance_criteria.when: the spouse questions continue
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee is asked whether the spouse or partner lives in Switzerland, with the answers "Switzerland" or "Another country", and must answer. The spouse's actual country is not collected. When the spouse is neither Swiss nor holds a C permit, the question is not asked, because the spouse cannot exempt the employee. The answer is recorded for source tax.

acceptance_criteria.title: Spouse exemption is decided from civil status and the spouse answers
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee has answered the civil status question and every spouse question that was asked
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio decides the spouse exemption
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee is exempt only if they are Married or in a Registered partnership and their spouse or partner is a Swiss citizen or holds a C permit and lives in Switzerland. In every other case there is no exemption, including Single, Divorced, Widowed and Separated employees, a spouse living in another country, and a non-Swiss spouse without a C permit.

acceptance_criteria.title: Spouse answers that no longer apply are not kept
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee has answered spouse questions
acceptance_criteria.when: they change an earlier answer so that the spouse questions no longer apply (for example civil status changed to Single, or they now answer that they hold a C permit) and then submit the questionnaire

stories.title: Decide whether the employee is subject to source tax
stories.i_want: Lonio to decide from the employee's answers whether they are subject to source tax, and to ask the source tax questions only of those who are
stories.so_that: I no longer have to work out by hand who must answer the source tax questions, and employees who are not subject are not asked for data no party needs

acceptance_criteria.title: Employees living abroad are always subject to source tax
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee's home address is in a country other than Switzerland
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio decides source tax liability
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee is subject to source tax whatever their nationality, even as a Swiss citizen. This includes residents of Germany, of Liechtenstein (see D-007) and of any other country.

acceptance_criteria.title: Employees living in Switzerland are subject only without Swiss citizenship, C permit or spouse exemption
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee lives in Switzerland and has answered the citizenship, C permit, civil status and spouse questions that were asked
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio decides source tax liability
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee is not subject if they hold Swiss citizenship (dual citizens included), hold a C permit, or are exempted by a Swiss or C-permit spouse or registered partner living in Switzerland. Otherwise they are subject to source tax.

acceptance_criteria.given: Lonio has decided whether the employee is subject to source tax

sections.title: Source tax tariff basics and computed result

stories.title: State the denomination for the church-tax part of the tariff

acceptance_criteria.title: Denomination is asked only from employees subject to source tax
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee has answered the residence and residence-status questions, and Lonio has determined whether the employee is subject to source tax (rule 'subject to source tax': everyone living abroad; in Switzerland only non-Swiss employees without a C permit who are not exempted by a Swiss or C-permit spouse living in Switzerland)
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee reaches the source tax details
acceptance_criteria.then: the denomination question is asked, and must be answered, only if the employee is subject to source tax; employees not subject to source tax are never asked it

stories.title: Determine the tariff letter, including the cross-border letters
stories.i_want: Lonio to determine the Zurich tariff letter for every employee subject to source tax from the answers already given (civil status, spouse employment, single-parent situation and cross-border situation)
stories.so_that: I no longer have to click through the Zurich calculator with the employee's answers to find the tariff letter

stories.title: Derive the calculator's residence answers from the home address
stories.i_want: the employee's state of residence for the Zurich tariff (Switzerland, Germany, Liechtenstein or another country) to be taken from the country of the home address, without asking the calculator's residence questions again
stories.so_that: each fact is asked once, and the right cross-border questions and base tariff follow from where the employee actually lives
stories.priority_reason: Lonio computes the tariff code itself (D-001). Without the state of residence, no tariff code can be computed for employees living abroad, and today HR has to work out the extra cross-border questions by hand (F-hr_transcript-ab8886).

acceptance_criteria.title: State of residence follows the home address country
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee has entered the country of their home address
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio works out the source tax state of residence
acceptance_criteria.then: Switzerland gives 'main residence in Switzerland'. Germany gives Germany, Liechtenstein gives Liechtenstein, and any other country gives 'other country'. The employee is not asked the calculator's 'Main residence in Switzerland?' or 'State of residence' questions.

acceptance_criteria.title: Switzerland and other countries get no cross-border questions
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee lives in Switzerland or in a country other than Germany or Liechtenstein
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee goes through the questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.then: no cross-border questions for Germany or Liechtenstein are asked, and the base tariff is used unchanged (for example A0N for a single person without children living in another country)

acceptance_criteria.title: Cross-border answers that no longer apply are discarded
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee answered cross-border questions for Germany or Liechtenstein and then changes the home address country
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee submits the questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.then: the cross-border answers for the country they no longer live in are discarded. Until submission they are kept, so going back and forth loses no input.

stories.title: Decide the cross-border tariff for employees living in Germany
stories.i_want: employees living in Germany to state what they expect for the year: whether they return home daily, whether they have provided a certificate of residence, whether a daily return would be reasonable, and whether they expect more than 60 work-related non-return days
stories.so_that: Lonio can decide, following the calculator, whether the cross-border tariff (A→L, B→M, C→N, H→P) or the normal tariff applies
stories.priority_reason: Without these answers Lonio cannot compute the tariff code for German residents (D-001). HR finds these questions the hardest part of the calculator (F-hr_transcript-ab8886).

acceptance_criteria.title: Daily return to Germany is asked of every employee living in Germany
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee's home address is in Germany. Living abroad makes them subject to source tax whatever their nationality.
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee reaches the source tax details
acceptance_criteria.then: they must answer 'yes' or 'no' to whether they expect to return daily to their main residence in Germany. The answer is recorded for source tax. Employees not living in Germany are not asked.

acceptance_criteria.title: Certificate of residence is asked only with daily return
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee lives in Germany and expects to return home daily
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee answers the cross-border questions
acceptance_criteria.then: they must state whether they have provided a German certificate of residence: 'yes', 'no' or 'not yet'. 'Not yet' is a valid answer. No document is uploaded; the certificate goes to HR outside Lonio. Employees who do not return daily are not asked.

acceptance_criteria.title: Reasonable return and non-return days are asked only without daily return
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee lives in Germany and does not expect to return home daily
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee answers the cross-border questions
acceptance_criteria.then: they must answer 'yes' or 'no' to whether a daily return would in principle be reasonable (less than 100 km driving distance). Only if it is reasonable, they must also answer 'yes' or 'no' to whether they expect more than 60 work-related non-return days in the calendar year. This is a declaration of what they expect, not proof.

acceptance_criteria.title: Cross-border tariff or normal tariff
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee lives in Germany and has answered the cross-border questions
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio computes the tariff code
acceptance_criteria.then: The cross-border tariff applies in two cases: daily return with a certificate of residence, or no daily return where a return is reasonable and no more than 60 non-return days are expected. In every other case the normal tariff applies, including a certificate answered 'no' or 'not yet'. For employees not living in Germany the cross-border tariff never applies. With the cross-border tariff the letter changes A→L, B→M, C→N, H→P. The result is always derived again from the latest answers. Paths not explored in the calculator are checked before go-live (see OQ-calculator-coverage).

stories.priority_reason: Lonio now owns the source tax result instead of HR's calculator run (D-001). Without these answers a Liechtenstein resident gets no result at all (D-007).

acceptance_criteria.title: Liechtenstein residents are asked the cross-border questions
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee's home address is in Liechtenstein. Living abroad makes them subject to source tax, so HR's rule decides that they are asked.
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee reaches the source tax details
acceptance_criteria.then: they must answer 'yes' or 'no' to whether they expect to return daily to their main residence in Liechtenstein. Only if they answer 'no', they must also answer 'yes' or 'no' to whether they expect more than 45 work-related non-return days in the calendar year. The answers are declarations of what they expect and are recorded for source tax. Employees not living in Liechtenstein are not asked.

acceptance_criteria.title: In principle no source tax liability, or normal tariff code
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee lives in Liechtenstein and has answered the cross-border questions
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio determines the source tax result
acceptance_criteria.then: Daily return, or at most 45 non-return days, gives 'in principle no source tax liability, subject to the double taxation agreement' instead of a tariff code. This result is recorded for HR with a flag; how HR sees and handles the flag belongs to the later HR-side spec. More than 45 non-return days gives the normal tariff code, subject to the double taxation agreement. For employees not living in Liechtenstein this rule does not apply. The result is always derived again from the latest answers.

sections.title: Completing and submitting the questionnaire
sections.purpose: Close the questionnaire. Remind non-Swiss employees and employees living abroad to bring their permit, and on submission record only the answers to questions that still apply.

stories.title: Remind employees to bring their permit on the first working day
stories.i_want: the questionnaire to remind every non-Swiss employee and every employee living abroad, at the end, to bring their permit on their first working day
stories.so_that: fewer new employees forget their permit on the first day (today about half of them forget), without collecting any additional data
stories.priority_reason: HR names a recurring pain ('Half of them forget'), but a forgotten permit does not block any registration; the reminder is a convenience that collects no data.

acceptance_criteria.title: Who sees the permit reminder
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee has answered the country of their home address and, if they live in Switzerland, whether they hold Swiss citizenship
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee reaches the end of the questionnaire, before submitting it
acceptance_criteria.then: the permit reminder is shown if the employee lives outside Switzerland (whatever their nationality, which is not asked of them) or lives in Switzerland without Swiss citizenship; it is not shown to a Swiss citizen living in Switzerland

examples.name: Tomás - Brazilian, B permit, lives in Winterthur (hr_transcript/F-hr_transcript-d7431e)
Stefan - Swiss citizen living abroad (hr_transcript/F-hr_transcript-1a20bb); country of residence assumed Germany

acceptance_criteria.title: The reminder collects no data and is worded by HR
acceptance_criteria.given: the permit reminder is shown to an employee
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee reads it and continues to submit the questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.then: the reminder asks for no answer, confirmation or document and records nothing; its purpose is to make the employee bring their permit on the first working day; HR provides the wording, which makes clear to a Swiss citizen living abroad that it does not apply to them

acceptance_criteria.title: No extra question only for the reminder
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee lives outside Switzerland
acceptance_criteria.when: the questionnaire decides whether to show the permit reminder
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee is not asked about their citizenship for the reminder's sake; the reminder is shown to them anyway

stories.title: Discard answers that no longer apply on submission
stories.i_want: answers to questions that no longer apply after I change an earlier answer to be kept while I move back and forth, but dropped when I submit
stories.so_that: I lose no input while correcting myself, and Lonio records no personal data about me that no receiving party needs
stories.priority_reason: Data minimisation is a core constraint of the feature (G-01): keeping answers no party needs means holding personal data Lonio must not have.

acceptance_criteria.title: Answers are kept while the employee goes back and forth
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee has answered follow-up questions and then changes an earlier answer so that those follow-up questions no longer apply
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee changes the earlier answer back before submitting
acceptance_criteria.then: the follow-up questions apply again and show the employee's earlier answers, so no input is lost

acceptance_criteria.title: Only answers to questions that still apply are recorded on submission
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee's latest answers mean that some questions they had answered earlier are no longer asked
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee submits the questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.then: the answers to the questions that are no longer asked are discarded and not recorded for HR or any receiving party; only the answers to questions that apply to the latest answers are recorded

examples.name: Employee changed civil status from Married to Single - spouse's date of birth is discarded
Employee changed home country from Switzerland to Germany - canton and citizenship answers are discarded
Employee living in Switzerland changed Swiss citizenship from no to yes - C permit and source tax answers are discarded

stories.title: Questionnaire is read-only for the employee after submission
stories.i_want: the questionnaire to become read-only for the employee once submitted, with every derived result always based on the latest recorded answers
stories.so_that: later changes go through HR only, and results such as the insurance start date and the tariff code never fall out of step with the answers (as happened with Julia's changed start date)
stories.priority_reason: Prevents inconsistent derived results after changes (a known incident with the insurance start date), but the HR-side change process itself is specified later.

acceptance_criteria.title: Employee cannot change answers after submission
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee has submitted the questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee wants to change an answer (e.g. after a move, a marriage, a new child, a certificate of residence handed in later or a corrected nationality)
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee can view but not change their answers; such changes are made by HR, which is specified in the later HR-side spec

acceptance_criteria.title: Derived results always follow the latest answers
acceptance_criteria.given: an answer recorded for an employee has changed after submission
acceptance_criteria.when: the derived results are looked at
acceptance_criteria.then: the insurance start date, the civil status for the pension fund and for source tax, whether the employee is subject to source tax and the tariff code are derived again from the latest answers; no history of earlier values is kept

stories.title: Send myself an email copy of my submitted answers
stories.i_want: to choose, when I submit the questionnaire, to receive an email with a copy of my answers at an address I type in
stories.so_that: I can look up what I entered myself instead of calling HR, who today get repeated calls from new employees asking what they entered
stories.priority_reason: HR reports a recurring nuisance ('New employees keep calling us to ask what they entered'), but the copy is optional and blocks no registration with any receiving party.

acceptance_criteria.title: Every employee is offered an optional copy at submission
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee has reached the end of the questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee submits the questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee is asked whether they want an email with a copy of their answers, answered with "yes" or "no"; the question may be left unanswered, and no answer means no copy is sent

examples.name: Employee is offered the copy at submission

acceptance_criteria.title: Email address asked only when a copy is wanted
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee is submitting the questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee answers whether they want a copy
acceptance_criteria.then: if the answer is "yes", the employee must type in the email address the copy is sent to; if the answer is "no" or the question is left unanswered, no email address is asked

examples.name: Employee does not want a copy

acceptance_criteria.title: The copy shows the submitted answers exactly, nothing more
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee has asked for a copy and typed in an email address
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee submits the questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.then: an email with a copy of the employee's answers is sent to that address; it shows the answers exactly as submitted (only the answers to questions that still apply, see the discarding of answers that no longer apply) and nothing more - no derived results such as the insurance start date, the civil status for the pension fund, the source tax result or the tariff code, and no other information; if the employee did not ask for a copy, no email is sent

examples.name: Employee asks for a copy and gives an address
Employee leaves the copy question unanswered

acceptance_criteria.title: The copy address is used only to send the employee's own copy
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee has typed in an email address for the copy
acceptance_criteria.when: the questionnaire is submitted and the copy is sent
acceptance_criteria.then: the address serves only to send the employee their own copy; it is not passed to the pension fund or to source tax, as no receiving party needs it. Whether the address is kept after sending or recorded for HR is open (see OQ-copy-email-retention)
